vsm1.4:127.1: In order to perfect the development of consciousness he should besides extend the counterpart sign according as acquired.
vsm1.4:127.2: Now, there are two planes for extension, namely, access and absorption;
vsm1.4:127.3: for it is possible to extend it on reaching access and on reaching absorption.
vsm1.4:127.4: But the extending should be done consistently in one or the other,
vsm1.4:127.5: which is why it was said “he should besides extend the counterpart sign according as acquired.”
vsm1.4:127.6: The way to extend it is this.
vsm1.4:127.7: The meditator should not extend the sign as a clay bowl or a cake or boiled rice or a creeper or a piece of cloth is extended.
vsm1.4:127.8:
He should first delimit with his mind successive sizes for the sign, according as acquired, that is to say, one finger, two fingers,
three fingers, four fingers, and then extend it by the amount delimited, just as a ploughman delimits with the plough the area to be
ploughed and then ploughs within the area delimited, or just as bhikkhus fixing a boundary first observe the marks and then fix it.
vsm1.4:127.9: He should not, in fact, extend it without having delimited the amount it is to be extended by.
vsm1.4:127.10:
After that has been done, he can further extend it, doing so by delimiting successive boundaries of, say,
a span, a ratana (=2 spans), the veranda, the surrounding space, the monastery,
vsm1.4:127.11:
and the boundaries of the village, the town, the district, the kingdom and the ocean,
making the extreme limit the world-sphere or even beyond.
vsm1.4:128.1: Just as young swans first starting to use their wings soar a little distance at a time, and by gradually increasing it
vsm1.4:128.2:
eventually reach the presence of the moon and sun, so too when a bhikkhu extends the sign by successive
delimitations in the way described, he can extend it up to the limit of the world-sphere or even beyond.
vsm1.4:129.1:
Then that sign appears to him like an ox hide stretched out with a hundred pegs over the earth’s ridges and hollows,
river ravines, tracts of scrub and thorns, and rocky inequalities (see M III 105)
vsm1.4:129.2: in any area to which it has been extended.
vsm1.4:129.3: When a beginner has reached the first jhāna in this sign, he should enter upon it often without reviewing it much.
vsm1.4:129.4: For the first jhāna factors occur crudely and weakly in one who reviews it much.
vsm1.4:129.5: Then because of that they do not become conditions for higher endeavour.
vsm1.4:129.6: While he is endeavouring for the unfamiliar higher jhāna he falls away from the first jhāna and fails to reach the second.
vsm1.4:130.2:
“Bhikkhus, suppose there were a foolish stupid mountain cow, with no knowledge
of fields and no skill in walking on craggy mountains,
vsm1.4:130.3:
who thought: ‘What if I walked in a direction I never walked in before,
ate grass I never ate before, drank water I never drank before?’
vsm1.4:130.4: and without placing her forefoot properly she lifted up her hind foot;
vsm1.4:130.5:
then she would not walk in the direction she never walked in before or eat the grass
she never ate before or drink the water she never drank before,
vsm1.4:130.6:
and also she would not get back safely to the place where she had thought, ‘What if I
walked in a direction I never walked in before … drank water I never drank before?’
vsm1.4:130.7:
Why is that? Because that mountain cow was foolish and stupid with no knowledge
of fields and no skill in walking on craggy mountains.
vsm1.4:130.9: he does not repeat, develop or cultivate that sign or properly establish it.
vsm1.4:130.10:
He thinks: ‘What if with the subsiding of applied and sustained thought I entered upon and dwelt in the second
jhāna, which is … with happiness and bliss born of concentration?’
vsm1.4:130.11:
He is unable with the subsiding of applied and sustained thought to enter upon and dwell in the second
jhāna, which is … with happiness and bliss born of concentration.
vsm1.4:130.12:
Then he thinks: ‘What if, quite secluded from sense desires, secluded from unprofitable things,
I entered upon and dwelt in the first jhāna, which is … with happiness and bliss born of seclusion?’
vsm1.4:130.13:
He is unable, quite secluded from sense desires, secluded from unprofitable things, to enter upon and dwell in the first
jhāna which is … with happiness and bliss born of seclusion. This bhikkhu is called one who
has slipped between the two, who has fallen between the two, just like the foolish stupid mountain
cow with no knowledge of fields and no skill in walking on craggy mountains …” (A IV 418–19).
vsm1.4:131.1: Therefore he should acquire mastery in the five ways first of all with respect to the first jhāna.
vsm1.4:131.2:
Herein, these are the five kinds of mastery: mastery in adverting, mastery in attaining,
mastery in resolving (steadying the duration),
vsm1.4:131.3: mastery in emerging, and mastery in reviewing.
vsm1.4:131.4: “He adverts to the first jhāna where, when, and for as long as, he wishes;
vsm1.4:131.5: he has no difficulty in adverting; thus it is mastery in adverting.
vsm1.4:131.6: He attains the first jhāna where … he has no difficulty in attaining; thus it is mastery in attaining” (Paṭis I 100),
vsm1.4:131.7: and all the rest should be quoted in detail (XXIII.27).
vsm1.4:132.1:
The explanation of the meaning here is this. When he emerges from the first jhāna and first of all
adverts to the applied thought, then, next to the adverting that arose interrupting the life-continuum,
vsm1.4:132.2: either four or five impulsions impel with that applied thought as their object.
vsm1.4:132.3: Then there are two life-continuum consciousnesses. Then there is adverting with the sustained thought as its object
vsm1.4:132.4:
and followed by impulsions in the way just stated. When he is able to prolong his conscious process
uninterruptedly in this way with the five jhāna factors, then his mastery of adverting is successful.
vsm1.4:132.5: But this mastery is found at its acme of perfection in the Blessed One’s Twin Marvel (Paṭis I 125),
vsm1.4:132.6: or for others on the aforesaid occasions.
vsm1.4:132.7: There is no quicker mastery in adverting than that.
vsm1.4:133.2: ability to enter upon jhāna quickly, as in the taming of the royal nāga-serpent Nandopananda (XII.106f.),
vsm1.4:134.1: Ability to remain in jhāna for a moment consisting in exactly a finger-snap or exactly ten finger-snaps
vsm1.4:134.2: is called mastery in resolving (steadying the duration).
vsm1.4:134.3: Ability to emerge quickly in the same way is called mastery in emerging.
vsm1.4:134.4: The story of the Elder Buddharakkhita may be told in order to illustrate both these last.
vsm1.4:135.1: Eight years after his admission to the Community
vsm1.4:135.2:
that elder was sitting in the midst of thirty thousand bhikkhus possessed of supernormal powers who
had gathered to attend upon the sickness of the Elder Mahā-Rohanagutta at Therambatthala.
vsm1.4:135.3:
He saw a royal supaṇṇa (bird) swooping down from the sky intending to seize an attendant
royal nāga-serpent as he was getting rice-gruel accepted for the elder.
vsm1.4:135.4: The Elder Buddharakkhita created a rock meanwhile, and seizing the royal nāga by the arm, he pushed him inside it.
vsm1.4:135.5: The royal supaṇṇa gave the rock a blow and made off.
vsm1.4:135.6: The senior elder remarked: “Friends, if Rakkhita had not been there, we should all have been put to shame.”
vsm1.4:136.1: Mastery in reviewing is described in the same way as mastery in adverting;
vsm1.4:136.2: for the reviewing impulsions are in fact those next to the adverting mentioned there (§132).
vsm1.4:137.1: When he has once acquired mastery in these five ways, then on emerging from the now familiar first jhāna
vsm1.4:137.2:
he can regard the flaws in it in this way: “This attainment is threatened by the nearness of the hindrances,
and its factors are weakened by the grossness of the applied and sustained thought.”
vsm1.4:137.3: He can bring the second jhāna to mind as quieter and so end his attachment to the first jhāna
vsm1.4:137.4: and set about doing what is needed for attaining the second.
vsm1.4:138.1:
When he has emerged from the first jhāna, applied and sustained thought appear gross to him
as he reviews the jhāna factors with mindfulness and full awareness,
vsm1.4:138.2: while happiness and bliss and unification of mind appear peaceful.
vsm1.4:138.3:
Then, as he brings that same sign to mind as “earth, earth” again and again with the purpose of abandoning
the gross factors and obtaining the peaceful factors,
vsm1.4:138.4: knowing “now the second jhāna will arise,”
vsm1.4:138.5: there arises in him mind-door adverting with that same earth kasiṇa as its object, interrupting the life-continuum.
vsm1.4:138.6: After that, either four or five impulsions impel on that same object,
vsm1.4:138.7: the last one of which is an impulsion of the fine-material sphere belonging to the second jhāna.
vsm1.4:138.8: The rest are of the sense sphere of the kinds already stated (§74).
vsm1.4:139.1: And at this point, “With the stilling of applied and sustained thought
vsm1.4:139.2:
he enters upon and dwells in the second jhāna, which has internal confidence and singleness of mind without
applied thought, without sustained thought, with happiness and bliss born of concentration” (Vibh 245),
vsm1.4:139.3: and so he has attained the second jhāna, which abandons two factors, possesses three factors,
vsm1.4:139.4: is good in three ways, possesses ten characteristics and is of the earth kasiṇa.
vsm1.4:140.1:
Herein, with the stilling of applied and sustained thought: with the stilling, with the surmounting, of these two,
namely, applied thought and sustained thought;
vsm1.4:140.2: with their non-manifestation at the moment of the second jhāna, is what is meant.
vsm1.4:140.3: Herein, although none of the states belonging to the first jhāna exist in the second jhāna—
vsm1.4:140.4: for the contact, etc. (see M III 25), in the first jhāna are one and here they are another—
vsm1.4:140.5:
it should be understood all the same that the phrase “with the stilling of applied and sustained
thought” is expressed in this way in order to indicate that the attaining of the other jhānas,
beginning with that of the second from the first, is effected by the surmounting of the gross factor in each case.
vsm1.4:141.1: Internal: here one’s own internal is intended;
vsm1.4:141.2: but that much is actually stated in the Vibhaṅga too with the words “internally in oneself” (Vibh 258).
vsm1.4:141.3: And since one’s own internal is intended, the meaning here is this: born in oneself, generated in one’s own continuity.
vsm1.4:142.1: Confidence: it is faith that is called confidence.
vsm1.4:142.2: The jhāna “has confidence” because it is associated with confidence
vsm1.4:142.3: as a cloth “has blue colour” because it is associated with blue colour.
vsm1.4:142.4: Or alternatively, that jhāna is stated to “have confidence” because it makes the mind confident with the confidence possessed by it
vsm1.4:142.5: and by stilling the disturbance created by applied and sustained thought.
vsm1.4:142.6: And with this conception of the meaning the word construction must be taken as “confidence of mind.”
vsm1.4:142.7: But with the first-mentioned conception of the meaning the words “of mind” must be construed with “singleness.”
vsm1.4:143.1: Here is the construction of the meaning in that case. Unique (eka) it comes up (udeti), thus it is single (ekodi);
vsm1.4:143.2: the meaning is, it comes up as the superlative, the best, because it is not overtopped by applied and sustained thought,
vsm1.4:143.3: for the best is called “unique” in the world.
vsm1.4:143.4: Or it is permissible to say that when deprived of applied and sustained thought it is unique, without companion.
vsm1.4:143.5: Or alternatively: it evokes (udāyati) associated states, thus it is an evoker (udi); the meaning is, it arouses.
vsm1.4:143.6: And that is unique (eka) in the sense of best, and it is an evoker (udi), thus it is a unique evoker (ekodi = single).
vsm1.4:143.7: This is a term for concentration.
vsm1.4:143.8: Then, since the second jhāna gives existingness to (bhāveti), augments, this single thing, it “gives singleness” (ekodibhāva).
vsm1.4:143.9: But as this single thing is a mind’s, not a being’s or a soul’s, so singleness of mind is said.
vsm1.4:144.1:
It might be asked: But does not this faith exist in the first jhāna too, and also
this concentration with the name of the “single thing?”
vsm1.4:144.2: Then why is only this second jhāna said to have confidence and singleness of mind?
vsm1.4:144.3:
It may be replied as follows: It is because that first jhāna is not fully confident owing to the disturbance
created by applied and sustained thought, like water ruffled by ripples and wavelets.
vsm1.4:144.4: That is why, although faith does exist in it, it is not called “confidence.”
vsm1.4:144.5: And there too concentration is not fully evident because of the lack of full confidence.
vsm1.4:144.6: That is why it is not called “singleness” there.
vsm1.4:144.7: But in this second jhāna faith is strong,
vsm1.4:144.8:
having got a footing in the absence of the impediments of applied and sustained thought; and concentration
is also evident through having strong faith as its companion.
vsm1.4:144.9: That may be understood as the reason why only this jhāna is described in this way.
vsm1.4:145.1: But that much is actually stated in the Vibhaṅga too with the words: “‘Confidence’ is faith, having faith, trust, full confidence.
vsm1.4:145.2: ‘Singleness of mind’ is steadiness of consciousness … right concentration” (Vibh 258).
vsm1.4:145.3: And this commentary on the meaning should not be so understood as to conflict with the meaning stated in that way,
vsm1.4:145.4: but on the contrary so as to agree and concur with it.
vsm1.4:146.1: Without applied thought, without sustained thought: since it has been abandoned by development,
vsm1.4:146.2: there is no applied thought in this, or of this, jhāna, thus it is without applied thought.
vsm1.4:146.3: The same explanation applies to sustained thought.
vsm1.4:146.4: Also it is said in the Vibhaṅga: “So this applied thought and this sustained thought are quieted, quietened, stilled,
vsm1.4:146.5: set at rest, set quite at rest,
vsm1.4:146.6: done away with, quite done away with,
vsm1.4:146.7: dried up, quite dried up, made an end of; hence it is said: without applied thought, without sustained thought” (Vibh 258).
vsm1.4:146.8: Here it may be asked: Has not this meaning already been established
vsm1.4:146.9:
by the words “with the stilling of applied and sustained thought?” So why is it said
again “without applied thought, without sustained thoughts?”
vsm1.4:146.10: It may be replied: Yes, that meaning has already been established. But this does not indicate that meaning.
vsm1.4:146.11:
Did we not say earlier: “The phrase ‘with the stilling of applied and sustained thought’ is expressed in this
way in order to indicate that the act of attaining the other jhānas, beginning with that of the second from the first,
is effected by the surmounting of the gross factor in each case?” (§140).
vsm1.4:147.1:
Besides, this confidence comes about with the act of stilling,
not the darkness of defilement, but the applied and sustained thought.
vsm1.4:147.2:
And the singleness comes about, not as in access jhāna with the abandoning of the hindrances, nor as in the first
jhāna with the manifestation of the factors, but with the act of stilling the applied and sustained thought.
vsm1.4:147.3: So that first clause indicates the cause of the confidence and singleness.
vsm1.4:147.4:
In the same way this jhāna is without applied thought and without sustained thought, not as in the third and fourth
jhānas or as in eye-consciousness, etc., with just absence, but with the actual act of stilling the applied and sustained thought.
vsm1.4:147.5:
So that first clause also indicates the cause of the state without applied and sustained thought;
it does not indicate the bare absence of applied and sustained thought.
vsm1.4:147.6: The bare absence of applied and sustained thought is indicated by this second clause,
vsm1.4:147.7: namely, “without applied thought, without sustained thought.”
vsm1.4:147.8: Consequently it needs to be stated notwithstanding that the first has already been stated.
vsm1.4:148.1: Born of concentration: born of the first-jhāna concentration, or born of associated concentration, is the meaning.
vsm1.4:148.2: Herein, although the first was born of associated concentration too,
vsm1.4:148.3:
still it is only this concentration that is quite worthy to be called “concentration” because of its complete
confidence and extreme immobility due to absence of disturbance by applied and sustained thought.
vsm1.4:148.4: So only this jhāna is called “born of concentration,” and that is in order to recommend it.
vsm1.4:148.5: With happiness and bliss is as already explained.
vsm1.4:148.7: Also second because entered upon second.
vsm1.4:149.1: Then it was also said above which abandons two factors, possesses three factors (§139).
vsm1.4:149.2: Herein, the abandoning of two factors should be understood as the abandoning of applied thought and sustained thought.
vsm1.4:149.3: But while the hindrances are abandoned at the moment of the access of the first jhāna,
vsm1.4:149.4: in the case of this jhāna the applied thought and sustained thought are not abandoned at the moment of its access.
vsm1.4:149.5: It is only at the moment of actual absorption that the jhāna arises without them.
vsm1.4:149.6: Hence they are called its factors of abandoning.
vsm1.4:150.1:
Its possession of three factors should be understood as the arising of the three,
that is, happiness, bliss, and unification of mind.
vsm1.4:150.2: So when it is said in the Vibhaṅga, “‘Jhāna’: confidence, happiness, bliss, unification of mind” (Vibh 258),
vsm1.4:150.3: this is said figuratively in order to show that jhāna with its equipment.
vsm1.4:150.4: But, excepting the confidence, this jhāna has literally
vsm1.4:150.5: three factors qua factors that have attained to the characteristic of lighting (see §119),
vsm1.4:150.6: according as it is said: “What is jhāna of three factors on that occasion?
vsm1.4:150.7: It is happiness, bliss, unification of mind” (Vibh 263).
vsm1.4:150.8: The rest is as in the case of the first jhāna.
